newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices firm, volume rises on demand.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices firm, volume rises on demand.

text.p: Prices on Istanbul's gold exchange edged higher on Tuesday in line with the trends in European markets, dealers said.
Traded volume was 1,064 kilos, up from Monday's 935 kilos on slightly firmer demand from the free market.
Gold closed up 3,500 lira and $0.50 at 1,112,000 lira per gram and $384.05 an ounce.
The lira which closed weaker at 89,830 to the dollar also fuelled gold prices in lira terms.
"Gold demand has been declining as the number of tourists and expatriate workers decrease after the summer," said a free market dealer.
"But there was excess liquidity in the free market. Most of it went to currency banknotes and some to gold," he added.
Traded volume plunged to 180 kilos in the afternoon from 884 in the first session. 86.4 percent of the total turnover was in lira terms. There were no dollar deals in the afternoon.
